newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES convertible bond to cover 5.4 pct of capital.
newsitem.headline: UES convertible bond to cover 5.4 pct of capital.

text.p: A 5.4 trillion rouble convertible bond to be issued by Russia's Unified Energy System (UES) with a projected 3-5 year maturity will be convertible into 5.4 percent of the national power utility's capital, an energy ministry official said on Thursday.

"The government share (in the capital covered) will be exactly 2.7 percent and there will be about 2.7 percent owned by UES," First Deputy Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko told reporters. Previously officials had said the volume of the bond would be five trillion roubles.
Kiriyenko said that proceeds from the half of the bond covered by the government stake would go directly to the government and be considered as privatisation revenue.

Proceeds from the RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) portion, which would be covered by existing UES shares controlled by UES, would also go to the government to pay UES's debts, he said. "These are not authorised shares," Kiriyenko said. "There will not be new issues."
Previously company officials had said the bond would probably be partly covered by some of UES's authorised but unissued capital.
Kiriyenko confirmed that the government had no plans to give up its controlling stake, which will be 50 percent plus one share after the bond conversion.
